question_en:
I am creating a one-page comparison of historical polar environment maps for a geography class. The attachment is cropped from an official monthly map, and its title and caption are missing. Please answer the following three questions:

1. Which official monthly map is the attachment from? Please locate the original map based on the image content and provide the publishing agency, product name, hemisphere shown, map type, and year-month.
2. In the complete original maps (1480×1591 pixels) archived for this product Version 4 from 2011 to 2025 for the same month, same hemisphere, same map type, and same base map style, in which years is the point at (800,330) located within the main white sea ice area? Coordinates are counted with the top-left pixel as (0,0), increasing to the right and downward.
3. The layout can only accommodate three historical maps. Using the statistics table for that same month from the same archive, select the three years with the lowest "Total Extent" values from the years identified in Question 2. List these three years and their "Total Extent" values in ascending order of value, and specify the unit.

Answer format: For Question 1, provide the publishing agency, product name, hemisphere, map type, and year-month in text. For Question 2, list all qualifying years in text. For Question 3, present a table listing the three years and values in ascending order of total extent, with the unit specified in the table header.
answer:
Question 1: Publishing Agency: NOAA@NSIDC / National Snow and Ice Data Center; Product: NOAA/NSIDC Sea Ice Index, Version 4; Hemisphere: Northern Hemisphere (Arctic); Map Type: September monthly sea ice extent map, high-resolution Blue Marble base map; Year-Month: September 2020.

Question 2: 2013; 2016; 2017; 2022; 2023; 2024; 2025.

Question 3:

| Year | Total Extent (million square kilometers) |
| --- | --- |
| 2024 | 4.35 |
| 2023 | 4.38 |
| 2016 | 4.53 |
